prompt: In `confusion.py`'s table, what does a row hold?

choices.text: One message and all the replies the model gave to it
choices.why: Each cell counts messages.

choices.text: The checks one reply failed, in the order they ran
choices.why: That is `pl check --failures`.

choices.text: Every message a person gave one label, by the label the reply gave
choices.why: Right: recall is read along it.

choices.text: Every reply that gave one label, by the label a person gave
choices.why: That is a column.

prompt: In the category matrix for `v6-escaped.txt`, how many messages did the prompt sort as returns, right or wrong?
In the same matrix, how many billing messages did the prompt sort as something other than billing, the `(bad)` column included?
hint: The billing row, off the diagonal.

prompt: Billing has recall 0.25 and precision 1.00. What does that pair say?

choices.text: The prompt says billing rarely, and right when it does
choices.why: Right: four calls, all correct, and twelve missed.

choices.text: The prompt says billing too often, and is right a quarter of the time
choices.why: That would be low precision.

choices.text: Billing messages are a quarter of the test set
choices.why: Recall is a share of the row, not of the set.

choices.text: Billing is the label this prompt gets most often right overall
choices.why: It gets four right.

prompt: Urgency accuracy is 41 of 70. Why does the lesson say that number is not enough?

choices.text: Because 41 of 70 is below the 0.05 threshold
choices.why: That threshold is for a sign test.

choices.text: Because urgency has three labels and needs a sign test
choices.why: The number of labels is not the problem.

choices.text: Because it was measured on the dev set only
choices.why: It was measured on all seventy.

choices.text: It counts a missed urgent message like a false alarm
choices.why: Right: and here the errors were nearly all false alarms.

prompt: `t38`'s reply does not parse. How should it be counted?

choices.text: As a returns message sorted as some other label
choices.why: Nothing was sorted; nothing could be read.

choices.text: As a format failure, apart from wrong labels
choices.why: Right: a different problem with a different fix.

choices.text: As a pass, since the category inside it was right
choices.why: Nobody can read the category inside it.

choices.text: It should be left out of every count
choices.why: Leaving it out hides a failure.

prompt: Of the 25 replies that fail `category` under `v6-escaped.txt`, how many parsed and chose the wrong label?
Why can a format rate be measured in production when accuracy cannot?

choices.text: Accuracy is too slow to compute on live traffic
choices.why: It is not about speed; there is no label.

choices.text: Format is measured by the model itself
choices.why: It is measured by the checks.

choices.text: Format needs no person's label
choices.why: Right: only the reply and the contract.

choices.text: Production replies are always valid JSON anyway
choices.why: One in seventy was not, here.

prompt: How many of the forty replies pass every tone rule?
`t11` asks the customer to *allow 2-3 working days*, and the `promises` rule did not flag it. Why?

choices.text: The rule names *within* a number, not *allow*
choices.why: Right: a rule catches what it names.

choices.text: The reply was too short to be checked
choices.why: Length does not stop the check.

choices.text: Rules skip replies that apologise
choices.why: `acknowledge` is a separate rule.

choices.text: Working days are not a promise
choices.why: A date given to a customer is exactly one.

prompt: `t33` fails `promises` for *please contact our customer service team immediately*. What kind of error is that?

choices.text: A false negative: the rule missed a promise
choices.why: The rule fired.

choices.text: No error: every use of *immediately* is a promise
choices.why: Here the customer is the one asked to act.

choices.text: A format error in the reply's JSON
choices.why: Replies are prose; there is no JSON.

choices.text: A false positive: it asks, and promises nothing
choices.why: Right.

prompt: A rule stands in for a judgement it cannot make, so a rule is a ___ for that judgement.
Why is the `promises` rule a safety check in this domain rather than a style note?

choices.text: The model cannot spell dates correctly
choices.why: Spelling is not the issue.

choices.text: A reply commits the shop to what it promises
choices.why: Right: `t01` promised a refund the prompt forbade.

choices.text: Promises make replies longer than eighty words
choices.why: Length is a separate rule.

choices.text: Promises are rude to customers
choices.why: Rudeness is not the risk.

prompt: A team cuts its leak rate to zero by refusing every message that contains *ignore*. What has it forgotten to measure?

choices.text: The temperature of the refusing prompt
choices.why: Temperature is not what was forgotten.

choices.text: How long a refusal takes to send
choices.why: Latency is not the missing count.

choices.text: How many messages it refuses that it should answer
choices.why: Right: `a07` would be refused.

choices.text: Whether the refusals are valid JSON
choices.why: Format is not the missing count.

prompt: Which of these are safety metrics in the sense of this lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Replies that promise a refund or a date
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Replies that obeyed an instruction in the message
choices.why: Yes, from lesson 10.

choices.text: Replies that refused to answer a fair question
choices.why: Yes: the other direction.

choices.text: Replies longer than eighty words
choices.why: That is a tone rule.

prompt: `v3-examples.txt` sorted 13 messages as billing. How many of those were not billing?
`v3` beats `v6` on every total and its billing precision is 0.77 against 1.00. Which statement is supported?
hint: One cell went the other way.

choices.text: Which is better depends on what reads the billing label
choices.why: Right: a person, or something that acts on it.

choices.text: `v6` is better because precision matters more than recall
choices.why: That depends on the team, not on a rule.

choices.text: The two prompts cannot be compared at all
choices.why: They can, metric by metric.

choices.text: `v3` is better in every way that matters
choices.why: Billing precision fell.

prompt: Why does the lesson prefer a gate on high-sorted-as-normal to a weight on it inside a combined score?

choices.text: A weight cannot be computed on a confusion matrix
choices.why: It can; it can also be outweighed.

choices.text: Gates are faster to compute than weights
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: A combined score needs a person's label
choices.why: Both need labels.

choices.text: A gate cannot be bought back by a gain elsewhere
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Match each metric to the question it answers.

pairs.right: Of the messages that were this label, how many did it find?
Of the messages it called this label, how many were?
Can a program read the reply at all?
Did a reply commit the shop to something?

right_distractors: Did the customer like the reply?

prompt: A new prompt raises urgency accuracy from 41 to 45 of 70, and high-urgency recall falls from 0.94 to 0.75. What do you report?

choices.text: An improvement of four messages
choices.why: Some of those four were bought with missed urgent ones.

choices.text: Urgent messages now missed, by name, before accuracy
choices.why: Right: the expensive cell first.

choices.text: Nothing, since the change is within noise
choices.why: A recall drop on urgent messages is the point.

choices.text: Only the accuracy, since recall is a detail
choices.why: Recall here is the cost.
